The transporter-erector-launcher (TEL) was first hit, damaging its Bashir 3D phased-array surveillance radar and Taer-2A surface-to-air missiles with a low-yield munition. A second strike followed, igniting fuel inside the missiles. The system was then finished off by a precision-guided bomb.

I can't make you surrender, but please do.
The irony is that Iran's Navy and Air Force were barely functional before the war started. Most of the aircraft hit on the ground weren't operational anyway, they were old airframes sitting in storage or being cannibalized for parts.
Iran is still operating F-4s and F-5s, as well as locally produced versions like the Saeqeh and Kowsar built by HESA, and none of them were destroyed. As for the navy, their doctrine is clear: they don’t focus on a traditional blue-water fleet. Instead, they rely on fast attack craft and coastal defense systems to operate close to shore.

The Chinese People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) has commissioned the guided-missile destroyer Tongchuan (hull number 177), a Type 052DL, into the 9th Destroyer Flotilla of the South Sea Fleet.
It is the 35th destroyer of the Type 052D series to enter service with the PLAN.
The DL variant is slightly lengthened by around 4 meters (about 13 feet), bringing the overall length to 162 meters. This gives it a larger flight deck, allowing it to operate heavier naval helicopters such as the Harbin Z-20F instead of the smaller Z-9.
